title: Ordered sequential execution of per-step function vectors
hypothesis: On held-out ordered compositions of structured state permutations, one shared neural executor conditioned on a different support-derived function vector at each step will match an external two-call executor and exceed an endpoint-only sum-of-vectors control, while using at least 35% fewer actual bytes than two untied step executors; it must also show a benefit over the same tied block with ordinary operator-ID embeddings to earn Mirror-specific credit.
physical_object: One shared width-32 neural state-transition block reused at every execution step.
mirror_coordinate: A support-derived 16-dimensional function vector for each primitive operator, supplied in ordered sequence to the shared block; hidden state is passed from one step to the next.
logical_multiplicity: Ordered compositions of two primitive functions from a shared library without storing a separate composed operator.

world.function_family: Affine bit permutations x -> permutation(x) XOR mask, closed under composition.
world.heldout_pair_split: Hash split ordered pairs; both orders are kept together in one split; atomic functions and all 16 states remain available for fitting.

model.primitive_executor: Shared MLP receives one-hot 16-state input and a 16d function vector; width 32 with one hidden layer, predicts next state.
model.function_vectors: Extract by averaging frozen shared hidden activation deltas over 8 support state-output pairs per primitive; task/function identity is not fed as a learned operator-ID embedding to candidate executor.
model.execution: Two ordered applications of the same block, with predicted intermediate argmax state passed to the second invocation and a distinct FV at each step.
model.native_tied_control: Same shared executor and update budget, conditioned on ordinary learned operator-ID embeddings instead of extracted FVs.
model.untied_control: Two independent step-specific transition blocks with the same function code interface.
model.endpoint_control: One-pass predictor conditioned on summed two FVs and initial state; no intermediate state feedback.
model.external_two_call_control: One-step shared block called twice by the host loop with explicit operator IDs and predicted intermediate state; count both calls and address inputs.
model.upper: Exact affine-function composition in structured code; charge serialized primitive parameters and executor metadata.

training.selection: Select common update/LR on dev by held-out ordered-pair accuracy for FV tied executor; apply it to every control.
training.paired_data: Same primitive support pairs, ordered pair split, minibatches and initialization seed streams across methods.

gates.PASS: All three fresh worlds and both dev worlds: FV tied executor reaches >=0.99 held-out pair exact accuracy, is within 0.01 of external two-call, saves >=35% actual bytes vs untied, and beats native operator-ID tied control by >=0.02 accuracy or >=20% bytes at equal quality.
gates.FAIL: Any quality, byte, or native-attribution gate fails.
gates.NOT_ESTABLISHED: Data split, execution order, replay, or payload accounting is invalid.

storage.authority: Actual uncompressed serialized inference payload bytes.
paid_objects: all per-primitive FVs or native operator-ID embeddings

boundaries: Synthetic affine rules only; no natural language or general task composition claim.
Two-step explicit execution is not a one-forward generation result.
Do not call ordered code counts independent capacity.
Fresh evaluation remains sealed unless all development conditions pass.

implementation_boundary.atomic_fit: One shared operator-ID-conditioned transition block is trained on all 16 states for each of 24 primitive affine maps. This makes atomic function coverage explicit before composition tests.
implementation_boundary.fv_extraction: For each operation, average pre-activation deltas h(state,operation)-h(state,null) over eight frozen support states. The resulting 16d FV is passed in place of the operator ID; the same trained state projection and output head are used.
implementation_boundary.native_alias_control: The native tied operator-ID method passes the learned operator embedding directly. Because the extracted FV may equal that embedding, exact functional aliasing is an expected Mirror-specific falsifier, not a protocol violation.
